question: What does nutrient quality primarily measure in a food item?

options.A: The total number of calories per serving
options.B: The biological usefulness of the nutrients provided
options.C: The shelf life and expiration timeline
options.D: The financial cost of the food item

explanation: Nutrient quality focuses on how well the body can utilize the essential components found in food, rather than just the caloric count. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h1)

question: Why is nutrient density more important than mere caloric density for a patient?

options.A: It supplies vital vitamins and minerals without excess empty calories
options.B: It guarantees immediate weight gain and muscle development
options.C: It lowers the financial cost of hospital meals significantly
options.D: It eliminates the need for any water consumption

explanation: Nutrient-dense foods deliver high amounts of essential elements per calorie, preventing deficiencies without overloading the patient with empty energy sources. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h1)

question: What defines a complete protein source?

options.A: Being derived exclusively from plant sources
options.B: Having zero fat content and high fiber
options.D: Containing all nine essential amino acids

explanation: Complete proteins supply all the essential amino acids that the human body cannot synthesize on its own. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h2)

question: A patient with type 2 diabetes needs advice on carbohydrate quality. What should the nurse recommend?

options.A: Refined sugars for a quick burst of energy
options.B: Saturated fats to slow down carbohydrate digestion
options.C: High-fiber complex carbohydrates to stabilize blood glucose
options.D: Low-protein starches to prevent kidney strain

explanation: Complex carbohydrates containing dietary fiber slow digestion and prevent the rapid blood glucose spikes seen with refined sugars. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h2)

question: What does micronutrient bioavailability measure?

options.A: The speed at which food passes through the stomach
options.B: The expiration date of vitamin supplements
options.C: The proportion of a nutrient absorbed and used by the body
options.D: The total weight of vitamins present in a raw food item

explanation: Bioavailability looks past ingestion to measure actual absorption and usability at the cellular level. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h3)

question: Which dietary factor enhances the absorption of non-heme iron from plant sources?
explanation: Ascorbic acid or vitamin C changes the chemical state of non-heme iron in the gut, making it much easier for the intestines to absorb. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h3)

question: Which group of nutrients is most easily lost during prolonged boiling in water?
explanation: Vitamins like C and the B-vitamins dissolve into cooking water and can be lost if the liquid is discarded. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h4)

question: Why does prolonged exposure to light and oxygen reduce the quality of certain nutrients?

options.A: It hardens the mineral structure making it indigestible
options.B: It increases the total carbohydrate count of the food
options.C: It causes the chemical breakdown of sensitive vitamins
options.D: It transforms unsaturated fats into complete proteins

explanation: Environmental factors like light and oxygen trigger oxidation and degradation of delicate vitamin structures. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h4)

question: A lack of dietary vitamin C over a prolonged period leads to which clinical condition?
explanation: Scurvy is the classic deficiency disease resulting from inadequate vitamin C intake, characterized by poor wound healing and connective tissue weakness. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h5)

question: Why can a patient with normal or high body weight still suffer from malnutrition?

options.A: Their body automatically destroys all ingested vitamins
options.B: Their diet may lack essential micronutrients and high-quality macronutrients
options.C: Fat cells store all necessary minerals permanently
options.D: High caloric intake neutralizes the need for proteins

explanation: Malnutrition encompasses poor nutrient quality, meaning a person can consume excess calories while remaining severely deficient in vital nutrients. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h5)

question: What is the primary focus of standard dietary guidelines for optimizing health?

options.A: Maximizing daily intake of artificial vitamin supplements
options.B: Choosing nutrient-dense whole foods over processed items
options.C: Reducing total fluid intake to prevent electrolyte imbalances
options.D: Eliminating all forms of dietary fat from the menu

explanation: Dietary guidelines consistently promote whole, nutrient-dense foods to supply adequate vitamins, minerals, and high-quality macronutrients. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h6)

question: When teaching a patient about healthy dietary patterns, what should the nurse emphasize?

options.A: Including a colorful variety of fruits and vegetables
options.B: Consuming foods with high sodium to retain water
options.C: Relying entirely on fortified meal replacement shakes

explanation: A diverse array of colorful produce ensures a wide spectrum of essential micronutrients and antioxidants. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h6)
